site.name: Malvina Mine
overview: The Malvina Mine was a prominent nineteenth-century telluride-gold mine in the Salina and Gold Hill mining area of Boulder County.
Federal mining history records its discovery in 1875 and substantial early production, while historic USGS topographic mapping preserves a named mine-level location for identification.

timeline.text: The Malvina lode was discovered during the summer of 1875 and quickly became one of the notable telluride-gold properties in the Salina area.
USGS historical reporting records rich telluride production and a shaft about 100 feet deep by the end of the mine's first year of development.
Boulder historical collections preserve underground-workings documentation and photographs associated with the Melvina/Malvina Mine, showing continued local documentation of the property.
The USGS Gold Hill 7.5-minute quadrangle retained Melvina Mine as a named mapped mine feature.

moreHistory: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 138 documents the Malvina as an important early telluride-gold producer in the Salina/Gold Hill area and records its 1875 discovery and development.

The 1957 USGS Gold Hill quadrangle explicitly labels Melvina Mine. A USGS/GNIS-derived mine point at approximately 40.049153, -105.384716 is used as the identification anchor; Remnant does not claim that this point is a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar.

Carnegie Library for Local History preserves Malvina/Melvina mine material, including an 1891 underground photograph. A focused media review did not establish a sufficiently clear app-use rights basis for packaging an exact-site historic image, so no image is attached.
